topics.topic: How unconfirmed cleanup is durably recorded, owned, identified, and completed before recovery re-executes, including for the start probe
questions: When the start probe itself has unconfirmed cleanup, what execution record is required, which module owns and writes it, and what record identity does it use, since the probe belongs to neither a run nor a trial case?

Before re-executing the element, how must startup deal with the previous environment whose processes may not have been reaped and whose exchange directory may not have been removed, and which module or durable record supplies the information needed to do so?

quotes: probe_sandbox: [RETURN_SHAPE] Returns None only when every check of its validation note holds — bwrap found, its version and the sandbox interpreter equal to the release's, and the probe execution succeeded; it writes no record.

execute_function: [SECURITY_BOUNDARY] MUST start bubblewrap with new user, PID, IPC, UTS and network namespaces and no network interface but the new namespace's own loopback, which bubblewrap brings up, with no capability option, the environment cleared and then set exactly to the imported SANDBOX_ENVIRONMENT constant, exactly the host paths of the imported SANDBOX_RUNTIME_PATHS constant bound read-only, inside the new root the symbolic links of the imported SANDBOX_ROOT_SYMLINKS constant (each name linking to its target, made by bubblewrap --symlink), one fresh private exchange directory bound read-write, bubblewrap's own fresh proc mounted at the imported SANDBOX_PROC_MOUNT constant and minimal dev mounts, and no other host directory; the child dies with its parent, and the runner is the init of the new PID namespace (bubblewrap --as-pid-1), so bubblewrap exits only after the host kernel has killed and reaped every other process of that namespace. The interpreter it starts there is os.path.realpath(sys.executable), the kernel's own CPython under a path of the imported SANDBOX_RUNTIME_PATHS constant, never a launcher such as a virtual environment's.

execute_function: [BEHAVIOR] An execution completes only after every process of the environment is reaped and the exchange directory is removed; every process counts as reaped once bubblewrap, started with --as-pid-1, has exited, and cleanup counts as confirmed only when both are; the function returns the judged result and neither raises StopRequiredError nor stops the process, which its caller does after recording the execution, and it never retries.
judgement.why: The later contracts decide that the startup probe writes no execution record and that sandbox owns per-execution cleanup while process lifetime and a fresh exchange directory prevent recovery from depending on a durable probe or environment-cleanup record.

topics.topic: Whether automatic recovery also applies to admission and explicit-try sandbox executions whose TrialExecution cannot be stored
questions: Is this automatic recovery limited to function elements of runs, or must it also repeat sandbox executions performed by admission or an explicit try when their TrialExecution cannot be stored?

quotes: try_implementation: [BEHAVIOR] MUST execute the named cases, or every case when none is named, in corpus order with execute_trial_case under the given actor, computes no verdict and activates nothing; a StopRequiredError stops at once and propagates.

admit_implementation: [VALIDATION_ERROR] A StopRequiredError from execute_trial_case stops the admission at once and propagates; no verdict and no activation are written, so the next submission runs admission again.

recover_running_runs: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST first call remove_run_spool for every run that has ended and keeps no spool — status succeeded, refused or cancelled, or failed with released_by set — ignoring a StoreInternalError of each removal; then MUST read every run that has not ended with one RunsByStatus naming running, awaiting_approval and pending (= models.RunStatus), whose answer is already oldest first in store order, and derive each again from its records under an Actor of kind kernel, as the behaviour note says.
judgement.why: The later contracts limit startup recovery to runs, require a new submission to restart interrupted admission, and provide no automatic restart of an explicit try after its propagated stop.

topics.topic: Whether recovery may re-execute after a store failure without preserving the first execution's mandatory immutable trace record
questions: Does this store-failure exception override K-09's requirement that every node execution writes one immutable trace record, or must the first execution still obtain a record before recovery may proceed?

quotes:
Every node execution writes one immutable trace record: run, node, pinned
versions, input and output by digest, verdicts, status, failure, resources, time.

If that record cannot be stored, the element has no concluded record and
  recovery executes it again, which A14 rule 5 makes safe for a function
  element: it has no effect.
judgement.why: K-09 requires a trace record for every node execution, while State 3 expressly permits a completed first execution to remain unrecorded and be repeated after restart.

basis:
An execution completes only after every process of the environment is reaped
   and the exchange directory is removed. If that cannot be confirmed the output
   is discarded, the execution is recorded `crashed` with detail
   `cleanup_failed`, and the kernel process stops; runs it left `running` are
   recovered on the next start (A14 rule 5).

If that record cannot be stored, the element has no concluded record and
  recovery executes it again, which A14 rule 5 makes safe for a function
  element: it has no effect.
